findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket for the prep area to measure roughly 75ppm quaternary ammonia. PIC was informed that the sanitizer was too weak, and the bucket was replaced. Ensure staff are changing the sanitizer buckets out frequently and testing with test strips to avoid using diluted sanitizer.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: Inspector found Tuna salad, made in house, at 51F when temperature was taken with a probe thermometer. The tuna salad was constructed and put to cool at 8am today. The probe temperature was taken at 2:15 pm. The tuna has been in the temperature danger zone for 6 hours and 15 minutes. The tuna salad will be discarded. The tuna salad is double panned in plastic with a tight fitting lid. Inspector suggests putting tuna in the walk in freezer to cool after it is constructed. Stir tuna salad in order to help remove heat from the salad. 5 lbs of tuna salad was discarded in the garbage. Take care to use effective cooling techniques such as covering lightly, single panning or placing in an environment that is cold enough to remove the heat from the product. The hang thermometer is reading 43F. The unit has been open on top for the lunch service period and appears to be going through a defrost cycle. These factors add up when cooling. Place tuna in a cooling unit when cooling not a make table. 

(A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The mop sink has areas where the caulk seal is missing. Seal the mop sink to the wall. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: Provide suitable location for storage of employee drinks. This location shall be low and way from food for sale to the public. 

(A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.
